narrative: The model estimated a 33.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning it saw about a one-in-three chance of repayment problems. That was enough to exceed the bank’s denial cutoff, even though it also implies a majority chance of good repayment. The decision was driven mainly by three factors. Your checking account status—listed as none, the most common category among approved applicants—was the most influential factor and actually worked in your favour. The second most important factor was your employment situation: being unemployed raised your risk, and only about 6.8% of approved applicants were in that category. The third factor was your savings balance below 100 DM, which also pushed toward bad credit, though it was a smaller influence and many approved applicants also have low savings. In short, the favourable checking-account signal was not enough to offset the employment and savings concerns. Next, ask the lender for a reconsideration review and provide updated employment information if your situation changes. Focus on securing stable employment and building savings before reapplying; you could also ask whether a smaller request or a guarantor would be considered. Avoid new debt in the meantime.
